tradingPermission.desc: How the agent handles orders at your connected brokerages. Paper orders are not affected. What you tell the agent in a conversation can narrow this, but only this setting lets orders skip your approval.

You can go back to approving each order at any time in Settings, and every order is recorded on the <orders>Orders page</orders>.

A provider that works with Claude Code serves the Messages API. One that works with Codex usually serves the Responses API, but some serve Chat Completions instead, so check its docs.
setup.customUnverifiedBody: How well a custom endpoint works depends on how fully it implements the API, which we can't test for each one. If the endpoint doesn't support prompt caching, long conversations get slower and costlier; if it sends requests to a different model, or ignores thinking or effort settings, you won't get what you picked; and if it's unreliable, requests fail more often.
setup.proxyUnverifiedBody: This address isn't {{provider}}'s own API or a cloud we recognize (AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI), so it's most likely a proxy, which we can't test. If the proxy doesn't pass prompt caching through, long conversations get slower and costlier; if it sends requests to a different model, or drops thinking or effort settings, you won't get what you picked; and if it's unreliable, requests fail more often.
